59.matn: Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated to us, he said: Fulaiḥ narrated to us, (change of chain) and Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir narrated to me, he said: Muḥammad ibn Fulaiḥ narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: Hilāl ibn ʿAlī narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abū Huraira, he said: While the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was speaking to the people in a gathering, a Bedouin came to him and said: “When is the Hour?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went on speaking. Some of the people said: “He heard what he said and disliked it.” Others said: “No, he did not hear it.” When he had finished his talk, he said: “Where is – I think – the one who asked about the Hour?” He said: “Here I am, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “When the trust (al-amāna) is lost, then await the Hour.” He said: “How is it lost?” He said: “When authority is entrusted to those not fit for it, then await the Hour.”
59.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who is asked about knowledge while occupied with his talk”. It is derived from it that the teacher may finish his talk before answering. In content, the hadith names the loss of trustworthiness, especially in the assignment of offices, as a sign of the Hour.

60.matn: Abū n-Nuʿmān ʿĀrim ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿAwāna narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Yūsuf ibn Māhak, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAmr, he said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, fell behind us on a journey we made. Then he caught up with us while (the time of) the prayer was pressing us and we were performing ablution. We began to (merely) wipe over our feet. So he called out at the top of his voice: “Woe to the heels from the Fire!” – two or three times.
60.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who raises his voice in (teaching) knowledge”. The hadith shows that the feet must be washed completely in ablution, and that repetition and calling out loudly can be appropriate in teaching.

61.matn: Qutaiba narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the trees there is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the Muslim. Tell me which it is.” The people thought of the trees of the desert. ʿAbdallāh said: It occurred to me that it was the date palm, but I felt shy (to say it). Then they said: “Tell us which it is, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “It is the date palm.”
61.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī brings the hadith in the chapter on knowledge; it shows posing questions as a teaching method. The palm resembles the Muslim in its constant benefit. Ibn ʿUmar’s restraint shows the courtesy of the younger towards the elders.

62.matn: Khālid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Sulaimān narrated to us, ʿAbdallāh ibn Dīnār narrated to us, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Among the trees there is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the Muslim. Tell me which it is.” He said: The people thought of the trees of the desert. ʿAbdallāh said: It occurred to me that it was the date palm. Then they said: “Tell us which it is, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “It is the date palm.”
62.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The imam poses a question to his companions to test their knowledge”. Testing questions stimulate reflection and consolidate what has been learned.

62.2.matn: Muḥammad ibn Salām narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Wāsiṭī narrated to us, from ʿAuf, from al-Ḥasan, he said: There is no harm in reading (the text) to the scholar. And Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf al-Firabrī informed us, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bukhārī narrated to us, he said: ʿUbaidallāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, from Sufyān, he said: When (a text) is read to the narrator, there is no harm in (the listener) saying: “He narrated to me.” He said: And I heard Abū ʿĀṣim say, from Mālik and Sufyān: Reading to the scholar and his own reading are the same.
62.2.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Not a prophetic saying but statements of early scholars in the chapter on knowledge. They attest the method of reading to the teacher (ʿarḍ), which in hadith transmission was recognized as equivalent to hearing from the teacher.
